21: type ReceiptsProvider interface {
22: 	// FetchReceipts returns a block info and all of the receipts associated with transactions in the block.
23: 	// It verifies the receipt hash in the block header against the receipt hash of the fetched receipts
24: 	// to ensure that the execution engine did not fail to return any receipts.
25: 	FetchReceipts(ctx context.Context, block eth.BlockID, txHashes []common.Hash) (types.Receipts, error)
26: }
27: 
28: type CachingReceiptsProvider struct {
29: 	inner ReceiptsProvider
30: 	cache *caching.LRUCache[common.Hash, types.Receipts]
31: }
32: 
33: func NewCachingReceiptsProvider(inner ReceiptsProvider, m caching.Metrics, cacheSize int) *CachingReceiptsProvider {
34: 	return &CachingReceiptsProvider{
35: 		inner: inner,
36: 		cache: caching.NewLRUCache[common.Hash, types.Receipts](m, "receipts", cacheSize),
37: 	}
38: }
39: 
40: func (p *CachingReceiptsProvider) FetchReceipts(ctx context.Context, block eth.BlockID, txHashes []common.Hash) (types.Receipts, error) {
41: 	if r, ok := p.cache.Get(block.Hash); ok {
42: 		return r, nil
43: 	}
44: 
45: 	r, err := p.inner.FetchReceipts(ctx, block, txHashes)
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return nil, err
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	p.cache.Add(block.Hash, r)
51: 	return r, nil
52: }
53: 
54: // CachedReceipts provides direct access to the underlying receipts cache.
55: // It returns the receipts and true for a cache hit, and nil, false otherwise.
56: func (p *CachingReceiptsProvider) CachedReceipts(blockHash common.Hash) (types.Receipts, bool) {
57: 	return p.cache.Get(blockHash)
58: }

70: func (f *BasicRPCReceiptsFetcher) FetchReceipts(ctx context.Context, block eth.BlockID, txHashes []common.Hash) (types.Receipts, error) {
71: 	fetcher := batching.NewIterativeBatchCall[common.Hash, *types.Receipt](
72: 		txHashes,
73: 		makeReceiptRequest,
74: 		f.client.BatchCallContext,
75: 		f.client.CallContext,
76: 		f.maxBatchSize,
77: 	)
78: 	// Fetch all receipts
79: 	// TODO: This is copied from the old implementation, but I'm not sure if this is
80: 	//   fetching sequentially instead of in parallel? The help text of Fetch says that
81: 	//   it is safe to call it concurrently, indicating that this should be done to
82: 	//   achieve parallellization, but there aren't any tests of Fetch calling it concurrently.
83: 	for {
84: 		if err := fetcher.Fetch(ctx); err == io.EOF {
85: 			break
86: 		} else if err != nil {
87: 			return nil, err
88: 		}
89: 	}
90: 	return fetcher.Result()
91: }
